paper_title: Birth Size and Breast Cancer Risk: Re-analysis of Individual Participant Data from 32 Studies
query: Evaluate the following scientific claim based on the literature: "Birth-weight is positively associated with breast cancer."
ground_truth: Verdict: SUPPORT. Evidence: Birth weight was positively associated with breast cancer risk in studies based on birth records (pooled relative risk [RR] per one standard deviation [SD] [= 0.5 kg] increment in birth weight: 1.06; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02-1.09) and parental recall when the participants were children (1.02; 95% CI 0.99-1.05), but not in those based on adult self-reports, or maternal recall during the woman's adulthood (0.98; 95% CI 0.95-1.01) (p for heterogeneity between data sources = 0.003).
claim: Birth-weight is positively associated with breast cancer.
evidence_spans: Birth weight was positively associated with breast cancer risk in studies based on birth records (pooled relative risk [RR] per one standard deviation [SD] [= 0.5 kg] increment in birth weight: 1.06; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.02-1.09) and parental recall when the participants were children (1.02; 95% CI 0.99-1.05), but not in those based on adult self-reports, or maternal recall during the woman's adulthood (0.98; 95% CI 0.95-1.01) (p for heterogeneity between data sources = 0.003).

paper_title: The Bile Acid Chenodeoxycholic Acid Increases Human Brown Adipose Tissue Activity.
query: Evaluate the following scientific claim based on the literature: "Chenodeosycholic acid treatment reduces whole-body energy expenditure."
ground_truth: Verdict: CONTRADICT. Evidence: In rodents, BAT can be activated by bile acids, which activate type 2 iodothyronine deiodinase (D2) in BAT via the G-coupled protein receptor TGR5, resulting in increased oxygen consumption and energy expenditure. Treatment of 12 healthy female subjects with CDCA for 2 days resulted in increased BAT activity.
claim: Chenodeosycholic acid treatment reduces whole-body energy expenditure.

paper_title: Combination varenicline and bupropion SR for tobacco-dependence treatment in cigarette smokers: a randomized trial.
query: Evaluate the following scientific claim based on the literature: "Combination nicotine replacement therapies with varenicline or bupropion lead to significantly higher long-term abstinence rates at 52 weeks than varenicline monotherapy."
ground_truth: Verdict: CONTRADICT. Evidence: At 52 weeks, 30.9% of the combination therapy group achieved prolonged and 36.6% achieved 7-day point-prevalence smoking abstinence compared with 24.5% and 29.2% in varenicline monotherapy (OR, 1.39; 95% CI, 0.93-2.07; P = .11 and OR, 1.40; 95% CI, 0.96-2.05; P = .08, respectively).
claim: Combination nicotine replacement therapies with varenicline or bupropion lead to significantly higher long-term abstinence rates at 52 weeks than varenicline monotherapy.
evidence_spans: At 52 weeks, 30.9% of the combination therapy group achieved prolonged and 36.6% achieved 7-day point-prevalence smoking abstinence compared with 24.5% and 29.2% in varenicline monotherapy (OR, 1.39; 95% CI, 0.93-2.07; P = .11 and OR, 1.40; 95% CI, 0.96-2.05; P = .08, respectively).

paper_title: Dexamethasone and risk of nausea and vomiting and postoperative bleeding after tonsillectomy in children: a randomized trial.
query: Evaluate the following scientific claim based on the literature: "Dexamethasone decreases risk of postoperative bleeding."
ground_truth: Verdict: CONTRADICT. Evidence: Two of 53 (4%; 95% CI, 0.5%-13%) children who received placebo had bleeding compared with 6 of 53 (11%; 95% CI, 4%-23%), 2 of 51 (4%; 95% CI, 0.5%-13%), and 12 of 50 (24%; 95% CI, 13%-38%) who received dexamethasone at 0.05, 0.15, and 0.5 mg/kg, respectively (P = .003).
claim: Dexamethasone decreases risk of postoperative bleeding.
